HTML Rendering Sample

This is the sample body for samples/html, used to verify that Reader + HtmlFileParser + HtmlRenderer can load and display an HTML file.

Checklist

  • Headings and paragraphs render completely
  • Scrolling feels smooth (default flipMode=scroll)
  • Choosing a local HTML file opens it again successfully
  • Images show placeholder first, then load when near the viewport
  • Inline images keep text line height; block images respect max width/height ratio

Sample Paragraphs

Spring water just born, spring woods just thriving; ten miles of spring breeze still fall short of you. The reader should place this full paragraph into the iframe content area and keep readable line spacing and margins. If you can see this sentence, the content injection path is working.

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat.

If loading succeeds, the toolbar status should show “Loaded”, and readable body text should appear here.

Images (lazy load)

The images below exercise HtmlImageObserver + HtmlImageLoader: placeholders first, then real sources when scrolled into view.

Inline icon next to text should stay on the same line without blowing up line height.

More Content (for scrolling)

Chapter 1: Morning light slips through the window lattice, and the letters on the page grow clear. Use the mouse wheel or trackpad to scroll down and confirm scroll mode works.

Chapter 2: Typography is more than placing characters on a page; it also gives the eye room to breathe. Paragraph spacing, heading hierarchy, and blockquotes are all part of readability.

Chapter 3: When you pick a local HTML file from the toolbar, Reader reopens it as a Blob. That bypasses the current parser path where a string URL does not download body content by default.

Chapter 4: To test paged mode later, set htmlOptions.flipMode to page in the sample and check whether page turns and page counts behave correctly.

Chapter 5: Before finishing, try “Reload” once more to confirm the same content can be opened repeatedly without leftover DOM from the previous load.

Chapter 6: After images load, open DevTools and confirm data-load-state becomes loaded, and blob URLs (if any) are revoked when the document is disposed.
